description:
About Focused Energy & SourceLight

Focused Energy is building the future of clean energy through laser-driven inertial fusion. As a spin-out of Focused Energy, SourceLight is turning breakthrough laser-driven radiation source technology into practical solutions for some of the world's most demanding inspection and material characterization challenges.

We are building on cutting-edge scientific innovation to develop scalable technology for industrial applications, including nuclear waste characterization, security screening, and non-destructive testing of safety-critical components.

As our technology moves from development toward industrial application, building a robust and scalable supply chain is essential to our success.

Your Role

We are looking for a Procurement & Supply Chain Manager to establish and lead this function from the ground up. This is a unique opportunity to take ownership of procurement and supplier strategy across the company, shaping how we identify, qualify, engage, and manage suppliers while ensuring our engineering teams have the components and resources they need to deliver.

You will work closely with our Product and Engineering teams, Finance, Legal, and external partners to establish company-wide procurement standards, negotiate complex technical and commercial agreements, and build a supplier ecosystem capable of supporting our growth.

Initially operating as a senior individual contributor, you will have significant autonomy and influence over how this function develops. title: GTM Engineering Intern | Revenue Operations (d/f/m)
description:
In a nutshell: 4 to 6-month internship in our RevOps team at our Munich headquarters (hybrid), starting between February and April 2027, with the opportunity to move into a full-time role straight afterwards.

About this role at Luminovo

Luminovo builds the B2B SaaS platform that powers the electronics supply chain. DACH is our home market and one of our strongest, and we have recently expanded into North America and the rest of Europe.

GTM engineering at Luminovo is part of Revenue Operations, the department that sits between marketing, sales and customer success and makes sure our revenue organisation runs smoothly.

Our go-to-market engineering function builds the systems that find the right companies and the right people for our sales team: target lists, data enrichment, hyper-personalised outbound campaigns that signal our sellers whom to call next. We work closely with Account Executives, the BDR team and marketing and directly contribute to pipeline generation.

As our GTM engineering intern, you will run outbound campaigns end to end and help build the next layer: signal-based lead generation. You will also help us improve account scoring and build AI automations that take manual work off our sales reps.

There is no textbook for this role. You will learn it the way we did: by building, shipping and seeing what works.

By the end of your internship, you will have shipped revenue systems that our sales & marketing teams rely on every day, and gained hands-on experience in go-to-market engineering, one of the hottest roles on the market right now!

You will also see first-hand how a modern B2B start-up operates day to day, with AI built into its workflows.

This role is for you

  • You combine technical thinking with commercial curiosity: perhaps you studied engineering and want to understand how companies sell, or you have discovered a passion for the commercial side of start-ups.

  • You are keen to work in a fast-paced environment and to grow alongside a high-growth start-up.

  • You bring the drive to learn quickly, a sharp analytical mind and the ambition to take on real responsibility from your first weeks. You collaborate well, ask questions without hesitation and are happy to get your hands dirty.

  • You use AI as more than a better search engine. You have built your own automations, workflows or tools, and can explain what you shipped and what came of it.

  • You are fluent in both German and English. Much of our outbound targets buyers in the DACH region, while the company operates in English.

  • You stand out if you have built something entrepreneurial during your studies, be it a side project, a student society or a small business.

  • You have first experience in GTM engineering, sales operations or automation (this is a big advantage but not a requirement!)

Your performance objectives

🧬 Run outbound campaigns

  • Deliver multichannel campaigns end to end. Build target lists, source and enrich the right contacts, and write the messaging in German and English.

  • Go where coverage is thin. Your campaigns will go wherever our sellers need the most support or wherever there is an opportunity worth pursuing, starting with DACH and extending to the rest of Europe and North America. Take on event campaigns, new regions and opportunistic plays, and turn them around to contribute to our pipeline.

🌀 Build signals and tooling

  • Ship signals. Build plugins or scrapers that generate high-intent leads for our sellers.

  • Process scaling. Transform website engagement into automated outbound triggers and create repeatable playbooks.

⚙️ Build automations

  • Remove manual work. Automate the repetitive manual tasks our revenue teams deal with day to day.

  • Challenge what exists. Get to know the systems we have built, then tell us where they fall short and help improve them.

💶 Unblock the sales team

  • Understand what sales reps need. Work closely with our AEs and BDRs, get to know their accounts and processes, and remove the friction that slows them down.

  • Close the loop. Feed what you learn from replies and campaign results back to sales and marketing.

🗂 Own the data

  • Own enrichment and imports. Take responsibility for account enrichment and every data import into HubSpot on contact, company and lead level.

  • Keep data accuracy high. You will be responsible for maintaining our enrichment so that data stays clean and workflows keep firing.

Your Toolkit

You will learn to work with the most modern sales automation tools on the market, such as Clay, n8n, Twain, Lusha, Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator and many more.

Work location

Our Munich headquarters. For your first two months you will be in the office most days, so you get to know the product, the team, our ICP and the basics of our market. After that, the role is hybrid, with the flexibility to work from home. Occasional travel for team retreats and industry events (expenses covered).

Whom you will be working with

  • Max Hungenbach, Revenue Operations Team Lead and your line manager

  • Danny Bodnar, GTM Engineer, your mentor and day-to-day coach

  • Clifton Lobo, VP Global Sales. You will work directly with him on GTM strategy.

  • Dasha Vyazemskaya, Head of BDR and your partner on handing campaigns over to the BDR team

  • George Knight, Demand Generation Manager in Marketing and your partner on campaigns run alongside marketing

  • Our Account Executives and BDRs across Europe and North America, for whom your campaigns run

Skills, knowledge, and expertise

Just so you know, we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. We care much more about your motivation and ability to help us accelerate technical progress than we care about your CV.

If you’re interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles, see here.

⚡️ About Luminovo

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry.

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress.

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain.

To date, over 300 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million.

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things

As a remote-first company headquartered in Munich, our brilliant team is spread across cities including Munich, New York, Austin, Calgary, Berlin, London, Valencia, Nairobi, and Verona, among others. 🌍

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. Among us are graduates from institutions like Stanford University and the University of Cambridge, as well as talented individuals with unconventional CVs. What matters most is their drive to build great things.

We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

title: Freelance Campaign Manager, Influencer Marketing, CPG (Europe) - Second European Language Essential
description:
About Kyra

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

Role Details

  • Freelance (up to 12 months)

  • Fully-Remote role across Europe or the UK

  • Fluency in a second European language essential

  • For this role, you must be fluent in English and at least one additional European language. This is an essential requirement.

We're looking for brilliant Campaign Managers who live and breathe the creator economy.

You'll be working with a leading global consumer brand, bringing creator campaigns to life across European markets.

And we're not talking about the occasional influencer campaign. This is creator marketing at scale. Multiple campaigns, regular product launches and a constant stream of creators producing content that gets people talking.

If you love discovering great creators, know what makes content perform and get excited about turning a brief into a successful campaign, we'd love to meet you.

At Kyra, we're building a different kind of creator marketing company. We combine great people, technology and AI to make creator marketing smarter, faster and more effective.

You'll have access to our own platform and tools to manage everything from casting and outreach to contracts, payments and reporting.

You'll take ownership of campaigns in your market, work directly with client stakeholders and collaborate with a team that genuinely loves what it does.

🚀 What You'll Be Doing

Bring Campaigns to Life

  • Manage multiple creator campaigns from the initial brief through to launch, delivery and reporting.

  • Keep timelines, budgets, content approvals and deliverables moving.

  • Work closely with creators, clients and our internal teams.

  • Spot potential issues early and find solutions before they become problems.

Make the Numbers Work

  • Build creator pricing around CPV targets and expected performance.

  • Negotiate creator fees and manage campaign budgets with confidence.

  • Balance creative ambition with commercial performance.

  • Use campaign data to make smarter decisions and improve results.

Build Great Client Relationships

  • Be a day-to-day contact for local market stakeholders.

  • Lead campaign calls, share updates and keep everyone aligned.

  • Bring ideas, recommendations and solutions to the table.

  • Build trust through great communication and consistent delivery.

Find and Work With Amazing Creators

  • Discover and cast creators who are the right fit for each product, audience and brief.

  • Build high-quality creator shortlists across multiple campaigns.

  • Manage outreach, briefing, negotiations, contracting and content delivery.

  • Oversee usage rights, advertising disclosures and creator approvals.

  • Use performance insights to make your next casting list even better.

Get Creative With Technology

  • Use Kyra's platform to manage campaigns from start to finish.

  • Monitor CPV, reach, engagement and other key performance metrics.

  • Use AI tools to make creator discovery, research, analysis and campaign management more efficient.

  • Keep campaign information accurate and up to date so everyone has visibility.

⚡ How We Work

We move quickly, work collaboratively and care about doing great work.

With multiple campaigns running at once, staying organised, taking ownership and communicating clearly makes a huge difference.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

  • New briefs are picked up within 24 hours, with creator discovery and outreach underway.

  • Blockers are escalated within 3 hours so we can resolve them quickly.

  • Campaign risks and performance concerns are raised early, ideally with a suggested solution.

  • Clients and teammates receive regular updates without needing to chase.

  • Campaign information is kept accurate and up to date in our platform.

We don't expect everything to go perfectly. We do expect people to take ownership, communicate openly and work together to find solutions.

🙌 Who We're Looking For

First and foremost, we want someone who really understands creator marketing.

Someone who knows the difference between a creator with a big following and one who can actually deliver results. Someone who enjoys both the creative and commercial sides of the job.

The Essentials

  • Languages: For this role, you must be fluent in English and at least one additional European language (e.g. Spanish, German or French). This is an essential requirement. You must be confident communicating with creators and clients in both languages.

  • 3–5 years of experience in influencer or creator marketing.

  • Experience running high-volume creator campaigns, ideally for consumer brands.

  • Strong knowledge of the creator landscape in at least one European market.

  • Experience managing campaign budgets, negotiating creator fees and handling contracts.

  • A solid understanding of CPV and creator performance metrics.

  • Strong Excel and data skills.

  • Experience working directly with clients, ideally large consumer brands.

  • Confidence using AI tools such as Claude in your everyday work.

  • Based in Europe or the UK, with availability to work across European business hours.

Even Better If You Have

  • Experience with CPG, FMCG or other major consumer brands.

  • Experience managing high-volume or always-on creator programmes.

  • Knowledge of multiple European creator markets.

  • Experience using influencer marketing platforms.

You'll Probably Love This Role If You...

  • Spend more time than you'd like to admit discovering new creators.

  • Can spot a great creator-brand fit almost immediately.

  • Love managing lots of moving parts without dropping the details.

  • Enjoy negotiating, solving problems and making the numbers work.

  • Get excited by technology and finding smarter ways to deliver campaigns.

  • Like having real ownership and seeing the impact of your work.

✨ Interested?

If you know your local creator market, love bringing great campaigns to life and speak fluent English plus at least one additional European language, we'd love to hear from you.

💬 Creator Communications

  • Own day-to-day comms with creators and creator managers, ensuring timelines, briefs, and expectations are crystal clear

  • Manage asset submission, revisions, and general troubleshooting throughout the campaign

🗂️ Project Management & Campaign Delivery

  • Run complex, high-value campaigns under the oversight of a Senior Campaign Manager

  • Build and manage detailed project timelines—ensuring alignment across Creator Partnerships, Paid Media, Strategy, and Client Solutions

  • Flag risks early and proactively manage challenges around creators, budgets, or shifting client expectations

👥 Client Liaison & Feedback Loops

  • Serve as a secondary point of contact for clients—attending calls, sharing updates, and supporting feedback management

  • Secure client approvals on key campaign milestones and keep them aligned throughout the process

📜 Creative Briefing & Content Review

  • Lead creator briefing calls and ensure deliverables follow brand guidelines, brief requirements, and FTC compliance

  • Review creator content for quality and accuracy prior to submission

📊 Performance Tracking & Optimisation

  • Monitor campaign KPIs and update trackers daily to ensure accurate performance records

  • Collaborate with internal teams to surface insights and make data-informed recommendations for optimisation

What Success Looks Like

✅ You’re managing campaigns with confidence, structure, and precision
✅ You’re keeping clients informed, creators aligned, and timelines on track
✅ You’re using data to optimise performance and guide decisions
✅ You’re delivering high-quality work that meets KPIs and strengthens client trust

title: Werkstudent Softwareentwicklung (m/w/d)
description:
Wir wollen eines der modernsten Gastronomieunternehmen werden. Und dafür entwickeln wir unsere Technologie selbst.

Vor Ort in Berlin · 15–20 Std./Woche · 17–20 €/Std. brutto · Start nach Vereinbarung

Wer wir sind

Nhas City Chicken ist eine moderne Halal-Chicken-Marke mit Standorten in Berlin und Köln. Was 1993 als Familienbetrieb begann, ist heute eine Marke mit eigenen digitalen Produkten – und einer klaren Vision: Wir wollen zeigen, wie moderne Gastronomie funktionieren kann.

Statt uns nur auf fertige Lösungen zu verlassen, entwickeln wir unsere eigenen:

  • NhasOS – unsere Software für den Betrieb: Schichtplanung, Zeiterfassung, Rechnungsfreigaben, Inventar. Beim Wareneingang erfasst das Team Mengen und Lieferschein-Foto, der Bestand aktualisiert sich automatisch.
  • Unsere Kunden-App für iOS und Android: Gäste wählen ein Zeitfenster, bestellen vor, zahlen in der App und checken per QR-Code ein.
  • Website in 10 Sprachen und Bestellportal mit Vorbestellung und Online-Zahlung.

Dabei arbeiten wir intensiv mit KI-Werkzeugen wie Claude Code – sie gehören bei uns fest zum Entwicklungsalltag.

Zeitfenster, Preise, Zahlungen, Lieferungen, Bestände: Überall steckt Logik, die stimmen muss. Und wir haben noch viel vor. Dafür suchen wir Studierende, die nicht nur Code schreiben, sondern mitgestalten wollen.

Was du bei uns machst

  • Neue Funktionen fürs Bestellportal entwickeln – im Frontend und in der API, die auch unsere Kunden-App nutzt
  • NhasOS weiterentwickeln, z. B. Rechnungsfreigaben, Inventar oder digitale Checklisten
  • Schnittstellen entwickeln und pflegen, z. B. die Kassenanbindung, die gerade entsteht
  • Tests für Zeitfenster- und Preislogik schreiben
  • Interne Abläufe automatisieren, etwa mit Python und APIs
  • Ideen von der ersten Skizze bis in den Restaurantalltag begleiten

Was du mitbringst

  • Du bist an einer Hochschule eingeschrieben – in Informatik, Wirtschafts- oder Medieninformatik oder einem anderen Fach, in dem du programmierst (z. B. Mathe, Physik, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen)
  • Erste praktische Programmiererfahrung und Interesse an modernen Webtechnologien – egal ob aus Uni, Job oder eigenen Projekten
  • Praktische Erfahrung mit KI-gestützter Softwareentwicklung: Du setzt Tools wie Claude Code, Cursor oder GitHub Copilot regelmäßig in deinen Projekten ein – idealerweise hast du schon intensiv mit Claude Code und agentenbasierten Workflows gearbeitet.
  • Du behältst die Kontrolle: Du nutzt KI gezielt von der Konzeption über die Entwicklung bis zur Fehlersuche und Optimierung. Den Code, den sie schreibt, verstehst du, prüfst ihn kritisch und entwickelst ihn selbst weiter – und neue Werkzeuge probierst du gern aus.
  • Du arbeitest dich selbstständig in Neues ein, fragst, wenn du hängst, und bringst eigene Ideen ein
  • Gute Deutsch- oder Englischkenntnisse. Deutsch ist ein Plus, weil du dich mit den Teams in unseren Restaurants abstimmst

Womit wir arbeiten: TypeScript, React, Next.js, Tailwind, Supabase, Stripe, Hono auf Cloudflare Workers, Vitest. Für interne Werkzeuge: Python. Du musst nicht unseren gesamten Tech-Stack kennen. Wichtig sind solide Grundlagen und die Bereitschaft, dich einzuarbeiten.

Du musst nicht alles können. Entscheidend ist, dass du etwas bewegen und dazulernen willst.

Warum Nhas

  • Eigene Technologie statt Standardlösungen: Die Probleme kommen aus dem eigenen Restaurant – die Lösung aus dem eigenen Code.
  • Software mit echtem Impact: Gäste bestellen damit vor, Teams erfassen damit ihre Lieferungen.
  • Mitgestalten statt nur abarbeiten: Du siehst im Betrieb, ob deine Lösung funktioniert – und verbesserst sie.
  • Ein Unternehmen mit großen Zielen: Vieles, was wir vorhaben, ist noch nicht gebaut – du baust es mit.
  • Raum zum Wachsen: Du vertiefst KI-gestützte Entwicklung an Software, die jeden Tag im Betrieb läuft.

Rahmenbedingungen

  • Vergütung: 17–20 € brutto pro Stunde, je nach Vorkenntnissen und praktischer Erfahrung
  • Arbeitszeit: 15–20 Std./Woche, möglichst flexibel und mit deinem Studium vereinbar
  • Arbeitsort: vor Ort in Berlin
  • Start: nach Vereinbarung
  • Betreuung: Du arbeitest direkt mit unserem Lead Developer zusammen

Bereit, mit uns etwas aufzubauen?

Wir suchen Menschen, die neugierig sind, gern Dinge entwickeln und Lust haben, gemeinsam mit uns an der Gastronomie von morgen zu arbeiten.

Zeig uns, was du kannst. Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung – ein GitHub-Profil oder eigene Projekte helfen, sind aber kein Muss. Ein kurzer Lebenslauf reicht.

Let's build what's next.

  • Hands-on familiarity with how insurers run claims, underwriting or pricing, and with the regulatory context (BaFin, Solvency II, EU AI Act)

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT

In this role, you will have the opportunity to shape the electrical architecture of a first-of-a-kind power plant and define how it interacts with both internal consumers and the wider electrical grid. You will drive the modernization of power system monitoring, diagnostics, and predictive maintenance strategies, leveraging data and digital technologies to improve reliability and operational performance. Beyond the plant itself, you will help develop innovative grid-facing capabilities and online services, exploring new ways for power generation assets to create value through advanced connectivity, flexibility, and participation in the evolving energy ecosystem.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Define and develop the plant's electrical architecture, ensuring reliable and efficient operation across diverse electrical loads and systems.

  • Lead grid integration studies and analyses, including load flow, fault, stability, power quality, and protection coordination assessments.

  • Specify and oversee the integration of electrical equipment, including transformers, switchgear, protection systems, and power conversion technologies.

  • Establish monitoring, diagnostics, and condition-based maintenance approaches to improve asset reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.

  • Develop predictive maintenance frameworks using operational and equipment health data.

  • Evaluate and develop opportunities for advanced grid services, including flexibility, ancillary services, demand response, and other emerging market offerings.

  • Explore innovative digital and online services that can enhance plant performance, operational visibility, and value creation within future energy systems.

WHO YOU ARE

  • You have a University (Higher education) degree in Electrical Engineering, Control Systems, Computer Science or equivalent

  • You have a strong background in electrical engineering, control systems, or a related field, with hands-on experience in industrial environments

  • You are adaptable and motivated to grow with evolving technologies and increasing system complexity

  • Experience in grid integration, or electrical infrastructure for industrial, utility-scale, or energy-related facilities is a plus

  • Knowledge of reactive power compensation is a plus

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

title: Senior LCA Engineer
description:
👷🏻‍♀️ What we do 👷🏻‍♀️

At Emidat, we are building the first climate-native product management system for building material manufacturers.

Emidat aims to decarbonise building materials, making up 11% of global GHG emissions. We collect data from physical production processes, generate a digital product passport with verified environmental data and make it usable along the value chain. In short: One solution to assess, design, buy, sell and manage products - with environmental impact at the core.

Embodied carbon is emitted on day zero and can never be reduced later, while global floor area is set to double by 2060. From January 2026, EU regulation (CPR) requires verified environmental data. 430,000 manufacturers will need it, and only about 2,500 have it today. That gap is our market.

Find out more about us, the team and our values here.

What you will work on

Your mission

Your core mission is to turn LCA methodology into software that works at scale. You own the full chain from methodological question to working software solution and take ownership of the team's most complex methodological and technical challenges. You make sure each new product category, market and verification takes less time and effort, working with high autonomy and high accountability.

As an early senior member of a fast-growing climate-tech company, your career trajectory is entirely in your hands. This role offers unparalleled visibility and growth. You can deepen your expertise as a technical expert in the team, or leverage your domain knowledge to pivot into high-impact roles across Customer Success, Sales, or Product. Exceptional early joiners are primed for future Team Lead and leadership positions.

In the first 6 months, you will

  • Lead strategic projects: Take full ownership of complex, ambiguous projects such as new markets, program operators or complex product categories. Define requirements, navigate trade-offs, delegate across the team and drive delivery.

  • Shape the product core: Work closely with our software engineers to translate environmental science and ISO/EN standards into clean, scalable software requirements, and propose complete implementation strategies for whole concepts, not individual features.

  • Scale our LCA work: Reduce the time and effort for recurring work such as tool verifications, new product category implementations and matching, through automation, reusable standards and better processes. Turn verifier feedback into requirements that solve the issue for good.

  • Scale tool verifications: Work with program operators and verifiers to establish processes that make tool verifications faster, more predictable and repeatable across markets and product categories.

  • Set the standard: Define what clear requirements and architecturally sound solutions look like, and take ownership of refining our methodologies for PCFs, LCAs and EPDs.

  • Improve how we work: Identify problems others don't see, turn them into actionable proposals, and solve recurring problems at the root instead of case by case.

  • Grow the team: Mentor junior colleagues and give them regular, actionable feedback.

  • Shape the industry: Help establish Emidat as a thought leader in LCA, e.g. by representing us in ECO Platform working groups and in the committees that author PCRs.

What you will bring to this role

Minimum requirements

  • Extensive LCA expertise: You bring deep expertise and experience conducting Life Cycle Assessments, LCA calculation methodology, PCRs and ecoinvent/matching logic. You showcase ownership of complex, ambiguous methodological or technical challenges.

  • Mastery of standards and regulation: You have comprehensive knowledge of the key LCA / EPD standards and program operator requirements (i.e ISO 14040/14044 and EN 15804+A2). You interpret these standards rigorously, and evaluate sources critically.

  • From methodology to software: You have experience working with automated software solutions for LCA/EPD generation, with proven ability to translate regulatory and methodological logic into technical requirements. You bring a product mindset: you prioritise, scope and communicate requirements clearly.

  • Verification and customer experience: You have created multiple EPDs that were successfully verified and published with a European program operator (e.g. EPD Global, EPD International, IBU). You have worked directly with customers, ideally in a consulting environment, and can represent methodological positions confidently towards customers and verifiers.

  • Leadership and project management: You have a track record of leading large projects end-to-end: scoping, planning, delegating, coaching others and keeping quality high. You manage several projects at the same time and coordinate multiple internal and external stakeholders.

  • Language: Business fluent in English (C1+).

Nice to have’s

  • Education: Bachelors, Masters Degree or PhD in a relevant subject, i.e Sustainable Energy Systems, Architecture, Urban Planning, Engineering (Environmental, Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical) etc.

  • Languages: Proficiency in German, or any other of the following European languages (French, Italian, Dutch, a Nordic language).

  • Verifier: Qualification as a verifier for EPDs acc. to EN 15804+A2

  • Engineering partnership: Experience completing partnering with software engineers to develop implementation strategies.

  • AI-enabled way of working: You are experienced in leveraging AI tools to accelerate your work, e.g. for research, requirements and documentation.

  • Tool Verifications: You have experience with EPD tool verifications.

  • Industry: Experience working on Construction products, or familiarity with the latest regulatory developments affecting the construction industry (e.g. EU Taxonomy, national and regional regulations) and can assess their impact on methodology and product.

title: Umschulung/Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker Systemintegration ab sofort (w/m/d)
description:
Über uns

Willst du mit uns gemeinsam eine der konservativsten Branchen überhaupt revolutionieren und in kurzer Zeit lernen, wie man exzellenten IT-Support leistet und ein Unternehmen mit Weitblick entwickelt? Dann verstärke unser Team im wunderschönen Herzen Oberfrankens, der Weltkulturerbestadt Bamberg.
Maximal Dental ist ein führendes Dental IT-Systemhaus, welches Zahnarztpraxen aus ganz Deutschland tagtäglich den Rücken freihält, um sich auf Ihr Kerngeschäft – das Wohl der Patienten zu konzentrieren. Unser Unternehmen vereint langjährig erprobtes Praxiswissen mit unkomplizierten Lösungsansätzen und kurzen Entscheidungswegen. Dadurch gelingt es uns Deutschlands Zahnarztpraxen zu digitalisieren und ihnen langfristig in allen Belangen rund um die IT-Sicherheit und den IT-Betrieb als starker Partner zur Seite zu stehen.

Suchst du einen Ausbildungsbetrieb, bei dem du nicht nur IT-Systeme, sondern auch dein Know-How auf das nächste Level hebst? Bei Maximal Dental in Bamberg wartet deine Chance, die Dentalbranche zu revolutionieren!

Aufgaben

Und so sieht Dein Spielfeld während deiner Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker für Systemintegration bei uns aus:

  • Mitwirkung bei der Durchführung von IT-Projekten - darunter Ausstattung von Zahnarztpraxen mit IT-Hardware und Telefonanlagen
  • Vor-Ort Installation, Konfiguration und Migration maßgeschneiderter Systemlösungen für die IT-Infrastruktur unserer Kunden (Serverumzüge, Client-Installationen, Netzwerkhardware, Firewalls, etc.)
  • Betreuung von Client-Server-Systemen (MS Windows Server, Active Directory, Branchensoftware)
  • Beantwortung von Helpdesk Anfragen rund um die Praxis-IT im per Telefon & Mail sowie über unseren zentralen Chat
  • Überwachung und Pflege unseres Netzwerk-Monitoring-Systems
  • Erstellung und Pflege von Netzwerkdokumentationen
  • Analyse und Beseitigung von Störungen und Anwenderproblemen
  • Unterstützung des technischen Support-Teams (1st und 2nd Level) während Leerlaufzeiten

Was erwartet dich sonst noch bei uns?

  • Du wirkst direkt aktiv im Team mit und kannst spielend Know-How aufbauen und festigen, z. B. in Aufgabengebieten der technischen Beratung oder in der Betreuung der IT-Infrastruktur
  • Du profitierst 100% von der fachlichen Förderung durch unsere IT-Experten

Qualifikation

  • Du hast mindestens den Realschulabschluss erfolgreich absolviert
  • Du bist technisch affin, kannst logisch denken und bringst Interesse an der Netzwerkadministration mit
  • Idealerweise hast du bereits erste Erfahrung im Umgang mit Windows Server Systemen oder PowerShell
  • Du bist begeisterungsfähig, zielorientiert und arbeitest am liebsten eigenständig
  • Du verfügst über einen Führerschein der Klasse B (optional)

Benefits

Deine Superhelden-Benefits:

  • Überdurchschnittliche Ausbildungsvergütung:
    1. Ausbildungsjahr: 1.050 EUR
    2. Ausbildungsjahr: 1.200 EUR
    3. Ausbildungsjahr: 1.350 EUR
  • Bonussystem: Zusätzliche finanzielle Superkräfte, leistungsorientiert.
  • 30 Urlaubstage: Erholung ist wichtig für jeden Helden.
  • Modernste Technik & Flexibilität: Arbeite mit High-Tech und genieße Home Office-Optionen.
  • Mega-Events: Feiere Erfolge mit uns auf Sommerfesten und Teamevents.
  • Corporate Benefits: Wähle zwischen Gutscheinkarten, Jobrad, Zusatzversicherung oder Fitnessstudio.
  • Lässige Atmosphäre & Flache Hierarchien: Sag 'Hallo' zu einem jungen, dynamischen Team.
  • Spannende Herausforderungen: Jeder Tag bringt neue Abenteuer.
  • Krisensicherer Arbeitsplatz: Sei Teil einer zukunftssicheren Branche.
  • Karrierechancen: Dein Weg nach oben ist frei.
  • Gemeinsames Frühstück: Standard bei uns.
  • Kaffee & Wasser: Superhelden müssen sich stärken, aber das ist ja selbstverständlich!

Bist du bereit, dein Cape anzulegen?
Dann schick uns deinen Lebenslauf. Deine Bewerbung behandeln wir streng vertraulich.
So startet dein Abenteuer:
Bewirb dich direkt, und innerhalb von 2-3 Tagen flattert unsere Antwort herein. Ein kurzes Telefoninterview, dann das persönliche Kennenlernen.
Noch Fragen? Florian Nestmann hilft dir jederzeit weiter.

description:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

 

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. 

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

title: Founding Customer Success Manager
description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The Role

We are hiring a Founding Customer Success Lead/Manager for the UK market.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who wants to build a market and a function, not simply manage a book of business or an expansion. You will work with some of our most strategic customers, helping them move from initial experimentation to broad, measurable adoption of AI across their organizations.

You will own the full customer journey, from executive alignment and implementation through long-term adoption, value realization, renewal, and expansion. You will build trusted relationships with C-level and VP-level leaders, help customers navigate the organizational change that comes with adopting AI, and turn successful customer outcomes into a repeatable Customer Success motion from our London HQ.

As our first senior Customer Success leader based at the London HQ, you will help define how Dust serves customers from the office. You will create playbooks, establish operating rhythms, shape our approach to executive engagement, and feed what you learn back into the wider Customer Success, Sales, Product, and Deployment teams.

Dust is an AI-native company, and that changes what Customer Success can look like. You will help customers understand how AI can reshape their work while using AI to make your own practice more effective, scalable, and precise.

This role is suited to someone who combines executive presence with a strong builder's mindset. You should be comfortable operating without a finished playbook, making decisions with incomplete information, and taking responsibility for outcomes from beginning to end.

What you will do

  • Own a portfolio of strategic enterprise customers, building durable relationships across executive, business, technical, and operational stakeholders.

  • Establish trusted-advisor relationships with C-level and VP-level leaders, helping them define their AI strategy and turn that strategy into meaningful business outcomes.

  • Lead complex customer journeys from kickoff through adoption, renewal, and expansion. You will coordinate the right people at the right time and make sure progress does not stall between teams.

  • Drive measurable value realization by helping customers identify, quantify, and communicate outcomes such as time saved, costs reduced, faster execution, and improved decision-making.

  • Lead executive business reviews and other strategic customer conversations, connecting product usage to business impact and creating a clear path to the next stage of adoption.

  • Support customers through enterprise-wide change management, including rollout planning, governance, internal enablement, use-case discovery, and the transition from individual experimentation to organization-wide adoption.

  • Identify and develop expansion opportunities across teams, functions, and geographies. You will partner closely with Sales to turn strong adoption and customer outcomes into sustainable account growth.

  • Orchestrate internal resources across Customer Success, AI Deployment Strategy, Forward-Deployed Engineering, Product, and Sales to deliver a cohesive customer experience.

  • Build the foundations of Dust's Customer Success motion from the London HQ, including account planning, executive engagement, adoption frameworks, value reviews, customer education, and feedback loops.

  • Represent the voice of customers inside Dust by turning customer needs, use cases, and patterns into clear product feedback, strategic insight, and better ways of working.

  • Contribute to the broader Customer Success team by sharing what works, raising the bar for strategic account management, and helping shape how a GenAI-native CS organization operates.

What we are looking for

  • You have 8+ years of experience in Customer Success, account management, consulting, solutions, or a related customer-facing role, with a strong track record of owning and growing strategic enterprise accounts.

  • You have worked with complex organizations where adoption requires sustained executive alignment, cross-functional coordination, and thoughtful change management over multiple quarters.

  • You have successfully managed senior customer relationships, including the ability to influence C-level and VP-level stakeholders and communicate credibly with business and technical audiences.

  • You have a track record of driving measurable customer outcomes, renewals, and expansion. You can move comfortably between strategic conversations and the operational details needed to make progress.

  • You have built or improved Customer Success processes, playbooks, or operating models. You know how to create structure where little exists and how to turn individual success into a repeatable motion.

  • You understand how technically sophisticated products are adopted inside large organizations. Experience with AI, developer tools, data platforms, enterprise software, or another emerging technology category is highly valuable.

  • You are fluent in AI concepts and are genuinely curious about how agents, language models, and automation will change the way companies operate. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should be able to engage confidently with technical teams and build practical AI fluency with customers.

  • You communicate with clarity and conviction in English, both in writing and in executive settings. French is helpful because you will work closely with our Paris-based teams, but it is not essential.

  • You have strong judgment, initiative, and ownership. You make sound decisions under ambiguity, follow through on commitments, and take responsibility for the outcome rather than waiting for perfect instructions.

  • You are comfortable being both strategic and hands-on. You can lead an executive business review in the morning, rethink an onboarding process in the afternoon, and write the first version of a playbook when the team needs one.

  • You are generous with context, direct in your communication, and committed to working as part of a team. You make the people around you better.

What success looks like

In your first six months, you will have:

  • Built strong relationships with the key executives, champions, and decision-makers across your customer portfolio.

  • Created clear account plans and adoption strategies for each strategic customer.

  • Established a repeatable approach to executive engagement, value realization, and expansion planning from the London HQ.

  • Helped customers move from isolated AI experiments to repeatable, high-value workflows used across teams.

  • Identified the most important customer and market patterns and turned them into actionable feedback for Dust's Product and Go-to-Market teams.

  • Created the first building blocks of a scalable Customer Success playbook.

Over time, you will help make Dust indispensable to some of the most ambitious companies and define what exceptional Customer Success looks like for an AI operating system.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

title: Product Marketing Manager
description:
Hi 👋 I'm Chris. I'm a Lead Product Marketing Manager at hx - I joined over four years ago as a Product Marketing Manager. Outside of work you'll find me playing sport (badly), watching reality TV, or taking my dog Lucky to the park (or the pub!).

Product Marketing at hx is a highly strategic function. We shape the company's positioning and messaging, decide where and when products launch, and build the process that gets them to market.

This role comes with deep ownership over how we address our core audience: actuaries. You’ll need to go deep into the life and workflow of highly technical users and develop messaging, positioning, and content that neatly conveys the benefits of our solution.

You'll need to be comfortable managing senior stakeholders and have great taste - but what matters most is drive, and a willingness to solve problems as you find them. In return, you'll join a team that's kind, supportive, and full of very smart people who want to go fast and far. If that sounds like you, read on!

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the team

Marketing at hx operates at the intersection of demand generation, systems thinking, and constrained markets. We build authority and demand in a highly technical, niche space where every account matters. This isn't template-driven volume work - it's deep, strategic B2B marketing crafted for a known universe of accounts, and we stay involved from first engagement through to customer success.

As Product Marketing Manager for Calculation Engines and Portfolio Intelligence, you'll sit at the heart of how hx becomes the obvious choice for actuaries who want to price faster and steer their portfolio with confidence. You'll own the technical story for our developer community - the most demanding audience we serve - and be the connective tissue between Product, Revenue, and the AI team, turning user insight into sharp positioning, useful sales assets, and narratives that stand up to scrutiny from people who'll know immediately if they don't. Your work spans two distinct challenges at once: deepening engagement and value realisation for our established Calculation Engines product, whilst driving launch readiness, early adoption, and strong feedback loops for Portfolio Intelligence.

The team experiments constantly, uses AI to focus on strategy over busy work, and operates with a high bar for quality and pace. You'll be joining a group that takes work seriously but not themselves, where compressed learning is the norm and the most future-ready in your craft is the standard.

Check out our Marketing & GTM Engineering Candidate Hub for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining!

What you'll be doing

  • Drive deeper engagement and adoption of Calculation Engines among existing users, using the usage data we now have to spot where users stall and creating messaging and enablement that moves them forward.

  • Own go-to-market execution for the Portfolio Intelligence release end to end - positioning, launch materials, enablement, and user communications that get it in front of the right people and drive real usage.

  • Accelerate early adoption of Portfolio Intelligence by creating onboarding support and launch assets that help target users get to first value quickly, evidenced by users moving out of the beta programme into sustained use.

  • Become the developer community's champion by writing technical content at a regular cadence that Solutions Engineering uses in live deals, and answering architecture and integration questions directly rather than routing them to Product.

  • Build hx's position in actuarial AI by developing differentiated positioning and up-to-date competitive understanding that works consistently across website copy, enablement, and customer conversations.

  • Establish strong feedback loops between users, Product, Revenue, and the AI team, so insight from launches, testing, and field conversations directly informs messaging, prioritisation, and product direction.

What you'll need to have done

  • Led product marketing in a B2B SaaS environment, balancing adoption work for an existing product with launch readiness for a new one at the same time - demonstrating commercial judgement across multiple GTM motions.

  • Increased engagement or adoption of a mature product by using user insight to sharpen messaging or enablement - with measurable improvement in usage, understanding, or qualitative feedback from users and revenue teams.

  • Owned a product launch end to end, including the internal readiness and enablement work that happens before it ships - not just the moment it goes out.

  • Turned a complex technical capability into credible, differentiated messaging for a skeptical, technical audience - developers or an equivalent evaluator population - built on real user insight rather than generic claims.

  • Worked hands-on alongside a Solutions Engineer or equivalent technical partner, comfortable being challenged on technical detail and holding your line, and earning trust across Product, Engineering, and Revenue without relying on formal authority.

  • Used AI with real judgement about when a technical claim is actually true rather than just plausible, and applied that judgement to rebuild how systems like enablement, competitive intelligence, or win/loss work - not just run them faster.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You expect full product maturity, clear roadmaps, and well-defined processes before taking action - hx moves fast and requires comfort operating in ambiguity where products, priorities, and messaging are still evolving.

  • You focus primarily on flashy launch work or brand campaigns rather than the detail-oriented, outcomes-driven work of deepening adoption, engagement, and user understanding.

  • You struggle to prioritise or make trade-offs without perfect information, waiting for others to decide rather than using judgment to move work forward with the context available.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  1. Initial call with our Talent team

  2. Hiring Manager Interview

  3. Skills Assessment & Panel Interview

  4. Values Interview

  5. Meet the CEO

  6. We offer!

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

title: Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy
description:
About Skyscanner

Everyone loves travelling, but planning is not without its challenges ✈️. That's why we've spent 20 years building tools that turn travel-planning chaos into a breeze. Today, around 160 million travellers count on us every month to skip the whole “47 browser tabs open” phase and find flights, cars, and hotels quickly and easily 💻.

Joining Skyscanner means becoming part of a global brand that's striving to become the planet's go-to travel hack accessible for all 🌍.

Our vision? To be the world's number one travel ally. (Ambitious? 💪Yes, but, hey, that's what got us here).

Now, we’re on the lookout for a Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy to help us bring that vision to even more travellers.

About the role
(Hybrid)

As our Principal Engineer for Identity & Privacy, you’ll shape the technical foundations that help us earn traveller trust while safely unlocking the data and AI capabilities behind brilliant product, personalisation, experimentation and advertising experiences.

This is a senior technical leadership role with impact right across Skyscanner. You’ll own the technical strategy and set standards for identity, consent and privacy engineering across our traveller-facing products, data platforms and operational systems — spanning web, app, backend, experimentation, analytics, advertising and machine learning.

What you’ll be doing

  • Setting our technical strategy: You’ll define and communicate the long-term vision and roadmap for identity, consent and privacy engineering, aligning it with our product strategy, traveller trust goals and data and AI ambitions.

  • Shaping identity at scale: You’ll lead our technical approach to purpose-scoped identifiers and consent-aware data processing across sessions, tracking, advertising, accounts, consent and derived identifiers.

  • Connecting the dots end-to-end: You’ll establish how identity and consent state flows from web and app surfaces through backend services, event streams and data pipelines to downstream consumers — making a complicated ecosystem feel a lot less complicated.

  • Turning privacy into engineering practice: You’ll translate privacy principles and legal guidance into reusable engineering patterns, platform controls, decision frameworks and measurable standards, including clear expectations around retention, deletion, masking, access control and auditability.

  • Leading across Skyscanner: You’ll partner with Engineering, Product, Legal, Privacy, Security, Data Governance, Data Science, Marketing, Ads and Analytics to navigate trade-offs, create clarity and turn ambiguous problems into decisions teams can deliver against.

  • Getting hands-on with the big stuff: You’ll provide technical leadership for large-scale initiatives spanning consent platform capabilities, privacy-safe experimentation, data retention and deletion, and traveller-trust features, while guiding teams towards simple, scalable, reliable and cost-effective solutions.

  • Raising the engineering bar: You’ll use observability, engineering health and incident learnings to improve how we operate, while coaching and mentoring engineers and championing high standards, constructive challenge and inclusive collaboration across our Engineering community.

About you

  • Privacy-engineering experienced: You’ve translated privacy and data-protection requirements — including GDPR, PECR, CCPA/CPRA or equivalent global frameworks — into practical engineering decisions, working effectively with Legal, Privacy, Security and Data Governance partners.

  • Built for scale: You’ve designed, built and operated large-scale distributed systems across identity, data platforms or adjacent areas such as consent, authentication, advertising technology or customer data infrastructure.

  • An influential technical leader: You’ve led significant technical change across multiple teams without direct line authority, creating clarity, alignment and momentum when ownership is distributed.

  • Strong in technical judgement: You’re comfortable making decisions where product value, traveller trust, privacy requirements, operational reliability and cost are all competing for a seat at the table.

  • End-to-end minded: You can reason confidently across client surfaces, backend services, event streams, data products, ML features, analytics, partner exports and operational tooling — and understand how a decision in one part of the system can ripple through the rest.

  • Practical about standards: You know how to turn policy into technical controls and measurable quality standards that teams can consistently use in real systems, rather than another document destined for a forgotten browser tab.

  • Clear, collaborative and credible: You can create shared engineering practices, write clear technical strategy and work effectively with senior stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Legal, Security and Data Governance. Familiarity with privacy and consent technologies, experimentation, personalisation, advertising measurement, Databricks, OpenTelemetry or SQL is valuable but not essential — as is practical experience using AI tools to make engineering work smarter.

What it's like here

We are the real deal - no corporate gloss, no empty promises. Just a team of genuinely curious, caring humans ❤️, building things that help travellers explore the world a little easier 🧭.

Skyscanner is made up of brilliant humans from every corner of the world. We believe travel makes the world better - and that the same is true of our diverse teams. Conveo is a Y Combinator-backed company in an active growth period. We're scaling past 100 people and delivering our 2027 hiring plan. The people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how this company is built.

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We're investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

What We’re Building

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high-quality consumer and B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Canva use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing and product teams.

Traditional research is slow, expensive, and superficial. Running it well requires expertise most teams don't have. That gap affects how well companies understand their customers and how well they can serve them. We're closing it.

The Role

As Talent Partner at Conveo, you will build the team that builds the company. You'll join a small, lean talent team and play a big part in how we scale. You'll play a key part in how Conveo attracts, assesses, and ultimately hires talent across the US, UK, and Belgium, helping us scale past 100 people and deliver our 2027 hiring plan.

You'll close exceptional talent across engineering, product, go-to-market, and operations, while contributing to hiring strategy and talent decisions. You won't be limited to one area. You'll work with stakeholders and leadership across departments. If your experience leans towards one area, such as product and engineering, go-to-market, or operations, that's fine. We're open to candidates with a variety of backgrounds.

This isn't a transactional recruiting role. You'll shape how candidates experience Conveo and help build a team with high talent density for the long term. Proactive sourcing and strong execution will be central to your success.

Talent operations plays a small part in this role. Lots of foundations are already in place, and you'll help build on them as we scale. If you like to experiment and work with the latest tech, especially AI, you'll find this role really interesting.

We're growing fast, so priorities shift and you'll often make calls with imperfect information.

What You’ll Do

Own hiring outcomes end-to-end

  • Partner closely with hiring managers and leadership

  • Own roles from kickoff to close, including sourcing and closing

  • Maintain speed without sacrificing quality

  • Develop strong hiring judgment

Build proactive talent pipelines

  • Develop centralised talent pipelines across key disciplines, enabling the business to take a broader and more proactive approach to hiring

  • Create innovative sourcing strategies for particular searches, incorporating AI-enabled sourcing, targeted outbound campaigns, market mapping, events, and external communities

  • Proactively source top-tier talent using LinkedIn, Juicebox, and other tools. Our toolkit isn't fixed. We're always looking at new tools, and deciding whether to build them internally or use them externally, to level up our sourcing and recruitment capabilities.

  • Provide external talent intelligence, including candidate availability, competitor activity, compensation, and wider market trends

Build a high-signal candidate experience

  • Be the main point of contact and advocate for candidates

  • Every candidate hears back from us quickly, whether it's a yes or a no.

  • Pitch Conveo with real conviction, because you understand the product, the market and why people join.

Grow our employer brand

  • Contribute to employer branding content that shows what it's like to work at Conveo

  • Support events that put Conveo in front of top talent

Build scalable hiring and people systems

  • Improve interview loops, scorecards, and decision-making

  • Track funnel health

  • Maintain clean hiring and people data in Ashby (our ATS) and internal tools

  • Build repeatable playbooks and templates

What Success Looks Like

  • Hiring managers see you as a true partner and want you on their searches: you've added key players to their teams quickly and efficiently.

  • Hires that work out: you bring in the right people, and we can see who was hired and why they did well in the organisation.

  • Ownership of our hiring goals: you understand the hiring plan and your contribution to it. When blockers come up, you flag them and proactively work to fix them so we hit our goals.

  • Gaps found and closed: you work autonomously, but take time early on to understand what gaps exist and why, then work with the team to close them.

  • Better decisions over time: you make decisions in the moment with the best information available, even when the data isn't perfect, and push to gather more data so future decisions are better informed.

  • A better way of doing things: you challenge the status quo when something could be done in a way that's better for the business, drawing on your experience and backing it up with data and resources.

Your First 3 Months

  • Hiring managers trust you as a partner and come to you early when they're planning hires.

What You’ll Bring

You're truth first, not fluff first: opinionated and thoughtful, with high standards and low ego. You're structured, fast, and iterative, and you build things once and make them reusable. You'll also bring:
